questions.topic: Structure: family, marriage, kinship, caste, tribe, ethnicity, religion, women
questions.question: The concept of ‘Sanskritisation’, the process by which a lower caste adopts the customs and rituals of a higher caste, was introduced by
questions.explanation: M.N. Srinivas introduced Sanskritisation in his study of the Coorgs (1952) and also the idea of the ‘dominant caste’. Louis Dumont wrote Homo Hierarchicus.

questions.topic: Structure: family, marriage, kinship, caste, tribe, ethnicity, religion, women
questions.question: Match the concept with the scholar associated with it: A. Little and Great Traditions B. Dominant caste C. Homo Hierarchicus D. Caste and Race in India — 1. M.N. Srinivas 2. Robert Redfield 3. G.S. Ghurye 4. Louis Dumont
questions.explanation: Redfield proposed Little and Great Traditions (applied to India by McKim Marriott); Srinivas — dominant caste; Dumont — Homo Hierarchicus (1966); Ghurye — Caste and Race in India (1932).

questions.topic: Structure: family, marriage, kinship, caste, tribe, ethnicity, religion, women
questions.question: Which of the following communities traditionally follow a matrilineal system of descent? 1. Khasi 2. Garo 3. Nair 4. Toda
questions.explanation: The Khasi and Garo of Meghalaya and the Nairs of Kerala (marumakkathayam) were traditionally matrilineal. The Todas of the Nilgiris are patrilineal and were known for fraternal polyandry.

questions.topic: Structure: family, marriage, kinship, caste, tribe, ethnicity, religion, women
questions.question: The rule that requires a person to marry outside his or her own clan or gotra is called
questions.explanation: Exogamy — marriage outside the clan, gotra or village. Endogamy — marriage within the caste or group. Hypergamy — a woman marrying into a higher-status group.

questions.topic: Social issues: casteism, communalism, regionalism, crimes against women, child labour, youth unrest
questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act prohibits employment of children below 14 years in all occupations except helping family enterprises after school hours. 2. Adolescents (14–18 years) are prohibited from working in hazardous occupations. 3. Article 24 prohibits employment of children below 14 in factories, mines and other hazardous employment. Which of the above are correct?
questions.explanation: All three are correct. The 1986 Act was amended in 2016 and renamed to cover adolescents; Article 24 is a Fundamental Right against exploitation.

questions.topic: Social issues: casteism, communalism, regionalism, crimes against women, child labour, youth unrest
questions.question: Match the Act with the year it was enacted: A. Dowry Prohibition Act B. Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) Act C. Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act D. Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act — 1. 1961 2. 1994 3. 2005 4. 2012
questions.explanation: Dowry Prohibition Act — 1961; PCPNDT (originally PNDT) Act — 1994; Domestic Violence Act — 2005; POCSO Act — 2012.

questions.topic: Social issues: casteism, communalism, regionalism, crimes against women, child labour, youth unrest
questions.question: Assertion (A): A declining child sex ratio is a serious social concern in India. Reason (R): Sex-selective abortion is driven by son preference and is prohibited under the PCPNDT Act, 1994.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: Both are true and R explains A. Son preference and the misuse of diagnostic techniques for sex selection are major causes of the falling child sex ratio (919 in Census 2011).

questions.topic: Welfare mechanisms: policies, programmes, constitutional & statutory safeguards
questions.question: Under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, consider the following: 1. The number of specified disabilities is 21. 2. Not less than 4% of vacancies in government establishments are reserved for persons with benchmark disabilities. 3. A ‘benchmark disability’ means not less than 40% of a specified disability. How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: All three are correct. The 2016 Act replaced the 1995 Act (7 disabilities, 3% reservation).

questions.topic: Welfare mechanisms: policies, programmes, constitutional & statutory safeguards
questions.question: Which of the following communities are notified as minorities by the Union Government under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992? 1. Muslims 2. Christians 3. Sikhs 4. Buddhists 5. Parsis (Zoroastrians) 6. Jains
questions.explanation: Five communities were notified in 1993; Jains were added in 2014, making six.

questions.topic: Welfare mechanisms: policies, programmes, constitutional & statutory safeguards
questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution empowers the State to make special provisions for women and children?
questions.explanation: Article 15(3) permits special provisions for women and children. Article 15(4) covers socially and educationally backward classes, SCs and STs; Article 21A is the right to education.

questions.topic: Welfare mechanisms: policies, programmes, constitutional & statutory safeguards
questions.question: The National Commission for Women was set up as a statutory body under an Act passed in
questions.explanation: The National Commission for Women Act, 1990 created the NCW, which was constituted in January 1992.
